newsitem.title: GERMANY: FORECAST - No major fall seen in German jobless rate.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - No major fall seen in German jobless rate.

text.p: German jobless rates are unlikely to fall much below the psychologically important ten percent level in 1996 and 1997, economists say, with some analysts forecasting rates of 10.5 percent by the end of 1997.

A Reuters survey published on Wednesday polled 29 economists on their views on German unemployment for the end of 1996 and 16 said they thought the jobless rate would fall from September's 10.4 percent to 10.3 percent.
Three economists thought unemployment would still be at 10.4 percent by the end of this year, while the upper-end forecast of 10.5 percent came from the London Business School.
The lowest forecast for the full-year 1996 unemployment rate, at 10.1 percent, came from Bank Julius Baer.

"Next year we will see moderate growth, initially led by exports and then by domestic factors. This will not have any real effect on the employment market," said Mathias Haffner, economist at BZW in Frankfurt.
The employment market is a lagging indicator of the fate of the market and it will be several years before it begins to mirror an upswing in the economy.
"The growth rate over the next one or two years is very low and with these levels of growth we are a long way from seeing any major turnaround in the unemployment figures," said Haffner.
As for 1997, economists were pessimistic about the prospect of any noticeable drop in jobless figures. The mean forecast for the end of 1997 was for a jobless rate of 10.1 percent.
Only six of the twenty-nine economists polled were optimistic that the jobless rate would fall below the ten percent level by the end of 1997.
In quarterly terms the outlook is similar. Economists see the employment rate in the fourth quarter of 1996 staying close to its current levels of 10.4 percent.

The lower-end estimates forecast a drop to 9.7 percent, while the upper limit is forecast at 10.5 percent. The mean forecast is looking for what amounts to a maintenance of the status quo at 10.3 percent.
